name: Annular Lichen Planus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Lichen Planus Variants

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic annular, violaceous, flat-topped papules or plaques with central clearing
Histopathological evidence of band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the dermoepidermal junction with basal cell degeneration
Presence of fine white reticulated lines (Wickham’s striae) on lesion surface
Exclusion of other annular dermatoses such as tinea corporis or granuloma annulare

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical identification of annular violaceous papules or plaques plus histopathological confirmation of lichenoid interface dermatitis and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is essential to differentiate from other annular dermatoses.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Annular violaceous flat-topped papules or plaques with central clearing
searchTerms: ring-shaped purple flat bumps with clear center
annular violaceous plaques with central clearing

pathognomonic.symptomName: Wickham’s striae (fine white reticulated lines on lesions)
searchTerms: fine white lines on skin lesions

common.symptomName: Pruritus localized to affected skin areas
Lesions predominantly on trunk and proximal limbs
searchTerms: rash mainly on trunk and upper arms
lesions mostly on body and proximal limbs
skin spots on torso and limbs

occasional.symptomName: Mucosal involvement with white reticulated plaques
occasional.notes: More common in classic lichen planus but can occur

occasional.symptomName: Nail changes including longitudinal ridging or thinning
Mild erythema and scaling at lesion periphery
searchTerms: mild redness and flaking at lesion edges
slight scaling and redness around rash

occasional.symptomName: Koebner phenomenon (lesions at sites of trauma)

rare.symptomName: Associated lichen planopilaris causing scarring alopecia
searchTerms: scarring hair loss from lichen planopilaris
hair follicle inflammation causing bald spots

laboratory: Histopathology showing band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at dermoepidermal junction
Basal keratinocyte degeneration with Civatte bodies
Absence of fungal elements on PAS stain
other: Direct immunofluorescence may show fibrinogen deposition along basement membrane zone

distinguishingFeatures: Positive fungal culture or KOH preparation
Scaling and active border with central clearing
Non-itchy annular plaques with smooth surface
Histology showing parakeratosis and neutrophilic microabscesses

redFlags: Rapidly progressive blistering or ulceration of lesions
Extensive mucosal involvement with pain or difficulty swallowing
Signs of secondary infection such as fever or purulent discharge
